title: MCP Phase 2 Roots Workspace Boundary Enforcement v1 — Rig Relay
files_changed: rig_relay/protocols/mcp/server.py (added workspace_root init param, _resolve_workspace_path, _assert_within_root; replaced all Path.cwd() usages with self._workspace_root in 5 filesystem-facing tools)

_resolve_workspace_path.rejects: path traversal (../), unresolved paths, paths outside root
_resolve_workspace_path.returns: tuple[Path | None, dict | None] — (resolved_path, None) on success, (None, refusal_envelope) on violation

_assert_within_root.returns: None if safe, refusal envelope if outside root

structured_refusal_behavior.path_traversal: Refused with root_scope_violation. No raw path leakage beyond the user-supplied relative input.
structured_refusal_behavior.symlink_escape: Refused at resolve() time — resolved path fails relative_to check.

remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_3_content_light: No output content-light scanning. File path hashes are used in dirty_state outputs but raw paths may still appear.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_4_evidence_envelopes: No common envelope wrapping. Responses lack session_id, request_id, surface, trace_id, etc.
remaining_mcp_phase_seams.phase_5_auth: MCPPerUserAuthorization model exists but not enforced. No per-session token required.

mcp_security_implications.before: Filesystem-facing MCP tools used Path.cwd() directly with no boundary enforcement. A client providing crafted path arguments could read outside the workspace.
mcp_security_implications.after: All 5 filesystem-facing tools check workspace root boundary before any filesystem access. Path traversal, symlink escape, and absolute-path escapes are refused with structured root_scope_violation refusals. Descriptor integrity verification runs before boundary checks.
